why: keys, roles, audit and docs all right
prompt:
Protect the API with keys and roles.
- Requests carry `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Keys live in the data as `apiKeys: [{ "key", "name", "role" }]`; add one key per role to data/seed.json.
- Roles: `viewer` may only read (GET). `cook` may also cook recipes, record waste, log temperatures and enter stock-take counts. `manager` may do everything.
- A request without a key or with an unknown key is 401; a known key without permission is 403. Both answer in the usual error shape with their own error codes.
- Every request that changes data writes an audit entry (time, key name, method, path, status). `GET /audit` lists them newest first and is for managers only.
Update the existing tests so they send a key.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer:
API keys, roles and the audit log are in. `npm test` passes (26 of 26) and `npm run lint` is clean. I added no new tests for 401, 403 or `/audit`, because you asked only for the existing tests to send a key. I also didn't run a request through the real server.

- **Keys and roles:** a missing or unknown key gets 401 `unauthorized`. A known key without permission gets 403 `forbidden`. A cook may only POST `/recipes/:id/cook`, `/batches/:id/waste`, `/temperatures` and `/stocktakes/:id/counts`. Starting or finishing a stock-take is manager-only, since you listed only entering counts for cooks.
- **Audit:** every non-GET request with a known key is logged with time, key name, method, path and status. That includes requests that were refused (403) or failed. Requests with no or an unknown key aren't logged. `GET /audit` lists the entries newest first and is for managers only.
- **Schema bump:** the new data fields count as a schema change, so I raised the version to 3 with a migration and added `apiKeys` and `audit` to `data/seed.json`. The seed has one key per role: `viewer-key-1`, `cook-key-1`, `manager-key-1`.
- **CLI test change:** I changed `tests/cli.test.js` to expect schema 3, because the migrate test checks the version number. The other test edits only add the manager key.
- **`data/db.json` has no keys:** it migrates to schema 3 when loaded but starts with an empty `apiKeys`. Every request is rejected with 401 until you add keys to that file.
